ui.articlesIntro: Practical guides to choosing products, checking details, planning costs and arranging shipping.
ui.faqIntro: 24 questions answered using official Pikobuy pages.

faq.question: What does Pikobuy do?
faq.answer: Pikobuy helps users source products from China, purchase from sellers, receive items at its warehouse and arrange international delivery. Its homepage describes these as separate stages of the service.

faq.question: Which marketplaces does the guide mention?
faq.answer: The official guide names Taobao, Tmall, 1688, Weidian and Yupoo. Check the exact product, size and colour before placing your purchasing order.

faq.question: How can I ask Pikobuy to find a product?
faq.answer: Pikobuy's homepage describes direct product search and submitting product links, images or sourcing requests. These are services on Pikobuy itself; they do not establish image-search functionality on this independent catalog.

faq.question: Why are purchasing and shipping separate payments?
faq.answer: The guide places the purchasing payment before warehouse inspection. You later choose a shipping route, submit the parcel and pay international shipping.

faq.question: Which payment methods can I use?
faq.answer: Pikobuy advertises multiple currencies and displays card and wallet logos, including Visa, Mastercard, Klarna, Google Pay and Apple Pay. Check your actual checkout for available methods, currencies and the total before paying.

faq.question: Will my order proceed if payment fails?
faq.answer: Pikobuy's terms say an order will not be processed when payment fails. Review the payment result in your account and use official support if the transaction status remains unclear.

faq.question: What happens when an item reaches the warehouse?
faq.answer: The guide describes warehouse check-in, photo confirmation and a defect check. Review the records for your own order before deciding what to ship.

faq.question: Do inspection photos guarantee authenticity or performance?
faq.answer: No. The user agreement explains that some products cannot receive professional quality or authenticity checks. Inspection may be limited to external condition and accessories. Photos are useful evidence, but not a universal product guarantee.

faq.question: Can I request more detailed inspection photos?
faq.answer: The forwarding terms say customers can view Pikobuy's inspection photographs or purchase additional detailed photos. Confirm the available photo service and charge within Pikobuy for the item you want checked.

faq.question: Can I request different packaging?
faq.answer: The shopping guide mentions minimal and reinforced packaging requests. Specify what you need and confirm the available handling options before submitting your parcel.

faq.question: Can items from different sellers share a parcel?
faq.answer: Pikobuy's contact page says items from different sellers can be combined into one parcel with one shipping charge. Compare the resulting parcel quote; this does not establish a guaranteed saving for every order.

faq.question: How long can my items stay in storage?
faq.answer: The forwarding terms confirm warehouse storage after receipt, but do not specify a universal free period or deadline. Check the current conditions for your items in Pikobuy or ask official support before waiting.

faq.question: What do I need for a shipping estimate?
faq.answer: Pikobuy's estimator asks for the destination, product type, weight, length, width and height. Use the best information available and check the final parcel quote before payment; a product listing price is not a shipping quote.

faq.question: Which shipping route should I choose?
faq.answer: Pikobuy advertises several shipping channels and route combinations. Compare the options currently available for your destination and parcel. The public About page does not establish one universally cheapest route or a guaranteed arrival date.

faq.question: When should tracking information appear?
faq.answer: The shopping guide says tracking information becomes available within three days after dispatch. Treat that as published guidance and contact Pikobuy about an overdue update.

faq.question: Can there be costs beyond the order and shipping?
faq.answer: Yes. Pikobuy's terms say cross-border orders may incur duties, taxes, brokerage or other charges borne by the customer. Check the applicable destination requirements and your chosen shipping terms before making a purchase.

faq.question: Can I forward items I purchased myself?
faq.answer: The forwarding terms describe obtaining a warehouse address from support or the forwarding form, submitting the required details, and waiting for receipt and photos. You then submit a parcel and pay shipping through Pikobuy.

faq.question: Who handles after-sales requests for forwarded items?
faq.answer: For items sent through forwarding, Pikobuy directs after-sales questions to the sender or seller. Its terms say it can help send the goods back, but does not provide the product's after-sales service.

faq.question: When must I request a warehouse return?
faq.answer: The return policy specifies 120 hours, counted from the hour after the status becomes In Warehouse. Apply promptly; acceptance still depends on eligibility.

faq.question: Is every product returnable?
faq.answer: No. Seller participation, resale condition and timing matter. Customized goods, altered packaging and certain product categories have restrictions. Check eligibility before ordering or removing tags.

faq.question: Are returns always free?
faq.answer: No. The policy lists shipping and service charges for customer-choice returns. Ask support for the order's exact total because the published shipping-fee wording is inconsistent.

faq.question: What if the seller sends the wrong item?
faq.answer: Report the mismatch through Pikobuy promptly. Its policy distinguishes seller errors and quality issues from customer-choice returns, but seller agreement and the specific case affect the outcome.

faq.question: Does a Not Shipped return request incur a fee?
faq.answer: The returns FAQ says it does not charge a return fee when the order has not shipped. Check the live status before making your request.

faq.question: Where should I ask about an order, payment or parcel?
faq.answer: Use Pikobuy's official Contact page, which recommends submitting a ticket and provides its support channels. This independent catalog cannot access your Pikobuy account, change an order or resolve a payment on your behalf.

articles.title: Pikobuy Spreadsheet Checklist: Compare Finds Before You Order
articles.description: Use a practical Pikobuy spreadsheet checklist to compare source links, variants, photos and budget, then decide which finds deserve a closer look.
articles.intro: A Pikobuy spreadsheet becomes useful when it helps you make a decision. A long saved list can hide missing sizes, stale links and costs you have not considered. The aim of this checklist is to turn several interesting finds into a small, explainable shortlist. Keep the current product listing separate from your own notes, and give every candidate a clear next action before you spend money.

sections.heading: 1. Define what the purchase must do
paragraphs: Start with the situation in which you will use the item. A bag for a laptop has a different requirement from a small bag for evenings. A hoodie for layering needs a different fit from one worn under a close-fitting jacket. Write one sentence that describes the job, then identify two or three requirements you cannot compromise on.

Set a total spending limit before looking at item prices. Leave room for the costs you still need to estimate. A product that fits your taste but cannot meet its practical requirement should not survive simply because the thumbnail is appealing.

sections.heading: 2. Save the identity of each candidate
paragraphs: Record the source URL, seller or store reference, exact option, displayed price and the date you checked them. Keep the size chart or important specification alongside that record. A spreadsheet title is often shorter than the full listing and may omit the variation that controls the price.

Use a short note for the reason you saved the item. For example, a candidate might match a required opening width or have the right sleeve length. If you cannot explain what makes it suitable, return to the requirement instead of adding more nearly identical rows.

sections.heading: 3. Identify what each image actually shows
paragraphs: A seller image describes how a product is presented. A photograph from an earlier buyer may show a previous order. Your own warehouse photographs relate to the item received for your order. Keep those evidence types distinct; their usefulness depends on the question you are asking.

A previous photograph might help you identify which detail to inspect, but it cannot establish the condition of a future purchase. Likewise, an attractive product image does not answer an unclear measurement question. Write the unresolved question beside the image instead of treating the existence of a picture as a completed check.

sections.heading: 4. Resolve essential gaps before ranking preferences
paragraphs: Check the requirements that could make the purchase unsuitable: item identity, available option, important measurements and a workable overall budget. If a source link opens a different product, or the selected size has no interpretable chart, pause that row.

Only compare preferences after those checks. Colour, finish and styling can help choose between suitable candidates; they cannot compensate for an opening too narrow for your laptop. Avoid a points system that lets several attractive features cancel one essential failure. A simple hold decision is often clearer than a misleadingly precise numerical score.

sections.heading: 5. Compare three hypothetical finds
paragraphs: This example concerns a bag that must accept a rigid object 30 cm wide. The values are invented to demonstrate the method, not taken from current products. Notice that the lowest displayed price does not decide which row deserves attention.

rows: External width is 34 cm; opening unknown
Hold: request the usable opening width
Opening is documented as 32 cm; budget incomplete
Keep for research: finish the total-cost estimate

sections.heading: 6. Give every saved row one next action
paragraphs: Use keep, hold and remove as research labels. Keep means the available evidence justifies the next step; it does not mean the item is verified or approved. Hold means one answer could change your decision. Remove means a requirement fails or the missing evidence is no longer worth pursuing.

Make the action specific enough to complete. Requesting the usable opening width is more useful than checking quality. Comparing the selected option price is more useful than looking at the listing again. Put a review date beside held candidates so the same unresolved items do not accumulate indefinitely.

sections.heading: 7. Recheck the shortlist before paying
paragraphs: Open the current listing again when you are ready to proceed. Confirm that the selected option, quantity and price basis still match the saved record. Revisit any measurement or availability claim that was supplied indirectly, and retain the evidence you actually used.

Then move into the ordering process with a concise record rather than a folder of disconnected screenshots. After warehouse evidence becomes available, compare it with that record. The same shortlist can now function as a check of what you intended to order, which details remain unresolved and what you should ask next.

articles.title: Pikobuy Clothing Size Charts: Measure Before Choosing a Size
articles.description: Read Pikobuy clothing size charts using a reference garment, consistent measuring points and clear units, with a worked example before you choose a size.
articles.intro: A familiar size letter is not enough to choose clothing from a Pikobuy find. The useful comparison is between measurements that describe the same thing: the same garment area, the same units and a similar method. This guide helps you build that comparison using clothing you already own. It does not assume every seller uses one sizing system or that choosing a larger letter fixes an unclear chart.

sections.heading: 1. Establish what the chart measures
paragraphs: Read the labels before interpreting the numbers. A chart may describe a finished garment, a recommended body range or a mixture of guidance and product measurements. Those are different references. A garment chest measurement includes the room designed into the clothing; a body measurement describes the wearer.

Save the chart with the exact product and selected version. If a listing contains different cuts or styles, do not assume one table applies to all of them. When the measurement type is unclear, ask for clarification before trying to convert the values into a size recommendation.

sections.heading: 2. Choose a useful reference garment
paragraphs: Pick an item that fits the way you want the new purchase to fit. Compare a relaxed hoodie with a relaxed hoodie, rather than using a fitted T-shirt as your only reference. Consider the fabric, shoulder construction and whether you expect to wear layers underneath.

Lay the reference garment flat without stretching it. Record the measurements yourself and keep a photograph showing the endpoints. You are building a repeatable comparison, so a careful note is more valuable than remembering that a particular brand usually fits you. Reuse the record only when the next product is genuinely comparable.

sections.heading: 3. Match the measuring points
paragraphs: For a top, useful measurements may include flat chest width, body length, shoulder width and sleeve length. For trousers, waist, rise, hip, thigh and inseam may matter. The correct selection depends on the fit problem you are trying to avoid.

Check how each dimension is defined. Sleeve length measured from a shoulder seam is not interchangeable with a measurement starting at the neck. A curved waistband and an elastic waistband also need an understood measuring method. If the seller uses a different endpoint from your reference, measure your garment again using that endpoint rather than comparing incompatible numbers.

sections.heading: 4. Separate width, circumference and units
paragraphs: A flat width runs across one side of a garment. A circumference describes a distance around it. Confusing the two can create a large apparent mismatch. As a simple arithmetic illustration, doubling a flat width of 58 cm gives 116 cm; whether that comparison is appropriate still depends on the garment and the chart's method.

Keep your worksheet in one unit and retain the original numbers beside any conversion. Do not infer an unstated tolerance. A seller's measurement tolerance, if provided, is additional context; it does not automatically explain every difference between a chart and a warehouse photograph.

sections.heading: 5. Compare two hypothetical hoodie sizes
paragraphs: Suppose your reference hoodie measures 58 cm across the chest and 68 cm in body length. The following invented chart shows why one size letter cannot settle the decision. Both dimensions matter, and the preferred result depends on which change you can accept.
list: Check sleeve measurements before choosing either option.
Confirm that all body-length measurements use the same endpoints.
Treat the table as a comparison exercise, not a size recommendation.

sections.heading: 6. Consider how you will wear it
paragraphs: A measurement match is helpful, but it does not reproduce the feel of a garment. Fabric stretch, stiffness, lining and cut can change how the same dimensions behave. Think about movement and the layers you intend to wear, then identify which measurements control those needs.

Avoid automatically adding a fixed allowance to every dimension. More width may help layering while extra sleeve length becomes inconvenient. If the chart leaves a critical dimension unanswered, request that measurement rather than relying on a general size-up rule. The purpose is to reduce a specific uncertainty, not create false precision.

sections.heading: 7. Preserve the decision and verify the option
paragraphs: Before paying, save the exact option label and the chart you used. Add a brief explanation of the decision, such as matching the reference chest width while accepting a shorter body. That note gives you a clear basis for later inspection.

If you request a warehouse measurement, state the dimension, endpoints and unit. A readable ruler should begin at the intended point and remain visible through the measurement. If the evidence contradicts the chart, pause and clarify the discrepancy while any available return process can still be considered. A photo can support a dimensional check; it cannot guarantee comfort.

articles.title: Pikobuy Product Links: Check Sources and Fix Listing Mismatches
articles.description: Check Pikobuy product links against their original listings, compare options after import and use a clear troubleshooting process when an item will not load.
articles.intro: A product link needs to identify more than an appealing image. It should lead to the intended listing and the option you plan to order. During sharing, shortening or conversion, that context can become harder to see. This guide gives you a practical way to preserve the source record, compare an imported result and decide what to do when a Pikobuy product link does not resolve as expected.

sections.heading: 1. Keep the original listing record
paragraphs: Before using a shared agent link, save the original product URL when it is available. Record the product identifier, seller or store reference, selected style, colour, size and quantity. Add the date you checked the listing and a screenshot of the option you intended to choose.

A screenshot alone is incomplete because it may omit the address or selected variation. A URL alone may not preserve which option you meant. Together, the link and a concise option record make it easier to identify a mismatch later. Do not overwrite the original record when you discover a different candidate.

sections.heading: 2. Identify the kind of page you have
paragraphs: A product page, a store homepage and a photo album serve different purposes. A store page can help locate a seller's catalogue but may not specify the item. An album may show several colours without giving a selectable purchase option. A product listing can contain many variations under one title.

Check which information is missing before attempting to import the link repeatedly. You may need an individual product link, a variant description or a clarification from the seller or platform. A recognisable marketplace name is context, not evidence that the page supplies everything needed for an accurate order.

sections.heading: 3. Compare the imported result with the source
paragraphs: Pikobuy's published guide supports searching with a product link or keywords. Once a result appears, compare its identity with your source record rather than assuming a successful load completes the check.

Look at the product identifier where visible, the seller context, available variations and the selected option's description. Check whether a displayed price refers to the item you want, a different variation, an accessory or a quantity condition. A similar thumbnail can conceal a different version. If the source and imported information disagree, resolve the disagreement before treating the result as ready to order.

sections.heading: 4. Understand what conversion does not establish
paragraphs: A link converter may help express a product reference in a form another service can read. That technical operation is separate from checking the seller, product condition, stock or suitability. It also does not establish that a current listing still describes the same item as an older saved row.

Keep the original URL alongside any converted URL. After conversion, repeat the identity and variation check. If a tool changes the destination unexpectedly, stop and inspect the result. Do not enter account credentials into an unfamiliar page merely because it was reached through a spreadsheet or a conversion utility.

sections.heading: 5. Diagnose the failure you can observe
paragraphs: The following table is a troubleshooting aid, not a list of official Pikobuy error messages. Use the actual behaviour you can see. Retrying is useful only when it tests a plausible cause; it does not recover information that was never present in the link.

rows: Compare source ID and selected variation
Keep both records and request clarification
Check the URL and visible product information
Use the legitimate source or official support
Only a shop or album opens
Look for an individual item reference
Provide the exact item and option details
Recover the original product URL if possible
Retry once with that source record

sections.heading: 6. Send a question that can be answered
paragraphs: When the intended item remains unclear, send the source link, product identifier if available, required option and a short explanation of the mismatch. Include screenshots that show the relevant selection. Avoid sending an entire browsing history or unrelated products in the same request.

A useful question is specific: this source shows the blue version in size M, while the imported selector only shows black; can the blue size M be ordered? That is easier to resolve than saying the link is broken. Pikobuy's official Contact page provides the appropriate route for account or sourcing questions.

sections.heading: 7. Record the outcome without losing context
paragraphs: Mark the candidate as matched, waiting for clarification or unavailable. Keep the response beside the source record. If the proposed alternative has a different product identifier or specification, start a separate row rather than quietly replacing the original item.

Before proceeding, recheck the actual option you will submit. The goal is a traceable decision: you should be able to explain which listing you used, which variation you selected and what evidence resolved any discrepancy. That record remains useful when you later compare the received item with what you intended to purchase.

articles.title: Pikobuy QC Measurements: Ask for Photos That Answer Your Question
articles.description: Make Pikobuy QC measurement requests more useful with clear endpoints, readable scales and focused questions before deciding whether an item meets your needs.
articles.intro: More photos do not necessarily provide more useful evidence. If you need to know whether a sleeve is long enough or a bag opening is wide enough, the request must explain how to measure that detail. A good Pikobuy QC request connects one unresolved question to one observable result. This guide shows how to make that connection without treating a photograph as proof of everything about the product.

sections.heading: 1. Write the decision before the request
paragraphs: State what answer would change your next action. Perhaps the item needs a minimum usable opening, the size label is unreadable, or a mark may be dirt rather than a shadow. Each issue calls for different evidence. Asking for better quality photos leaves the person taking them to guess what matters.
Use a sentence with an observable detail: I need to see whether both shoes carry the selected size label. Avoid combining that with unrelated requests about stitching, materials and packing.

sections.heading: 2. Identify the correct item and option
paragraphs: Include the relevant order reference, item description and selected variation. If the order contains two similar colours or sizes, make the distinction explicit. Refer to an existing photo when it helps identify the area, but do not assume an earlier buyer's image shows the item currently being inspected.

Keep your source chart and intended option beside the request. They explain why a measurement matters and help you interpret the result. An accurate measurement of the wrong item is still unusable. Before drawing a conclusion, check that the returned image can reasonably be connected to the item and variation you asked about.

sections.heading: 3. Describe the measuring method
paragraphs: Name the endpoints, unit and position. For flat garment width, specify where the tape should start and end and whether the garment should lie flat without stretching. For a bag opening, ask for the usable span at the opening rather than the widest external part of the bag.

Ask for the start and finish of the scale to be visible. An image with the zero point outside the frame creates uncertainty even when the far end looks readable. Measurements along a curve and straight-line measurements answer different questions, so explain which one you need rather than using the word length alone.

sections.heading: 4. Use a request that matches the question
paragraphs: These examples are original wording templates, not menu options or promises of a particular service. Confirm whether the requested handling is available and what it costs before relying on it. Replace the item and measurement details with those relevant to your order.

rows: Lay the selected top flat without stretching and show chest width between the stated points, with both ends of the centimetre scale visible.
Show a readable size label from each shoe in this pair, with enough surrounding detail to identify the items.
Will an object pass through the bag opening?
Show the usable opening width with the closure fully open and the measuring endpoints visible.
Is the mark on the surface?
Show the marked area in a closer view and another angle, with the surrounding material visible.

sections.heading: 5. Check whether the response is interpretable
paragraphs: Read the image before reading the numerical conclusion. Is the relevant item visible? Does the ruler follow the method you requested? Can you see the scale and both endpoints? If the garment is folded, stretched or photographed at a strong angle, note how that could affect the comparison.

Do not manufacture precision from a blurry image. If you can only distinguish approximately 57 to 59 cm, record that uncertainty rather than declaring 58.0 cm. When the uncertainty is large enough to change the decision, request clarification. When it cannot affect the decision, additional photos may provide little practical value.

sections.heading: 6. Keep visual evidence within its limits
paragraphs: A photograph can support a conclusion about a visible label, a measured dimension or an apparent surface issue. It cannot establish long-term durability, hidden construction, electrical performance or comfort during use. Material composition and authenticity also require evidence beyond appearance alone.

Separate what you observed from what you inferred. The image shows a closed seam is a narrower statement than the bag will withstand heavy loads. Pikobuy's published materials describe inspection limitations, so avoid treating inspection as specialist testing. If a purchase depends on a property that photographs cannot establish, seek suitable documentation or reconsider the purchase.

sections.heading: 7. Turn the answer into an action
paragraphs: Return to the original question and choose a next step. The evidence may support proceeding, leave a specific issue unresolved or justify discussing a return. Save the response with the order record and note which measurement or visible detail informed your decision.

If a problem remains, check the current order status and applicable return conditions promptly. Do not spend time collecting decorative angles while an actionable mismatch goes unreported. Your record should make the issue easy to explain: what was intended, what the photograph shows and what resolution you are requesting. Keep uncertain observations labelled as uncertain.

sections.heading: 8. Turn the measurement into a clear decision
paragraphs: Compare the photographed measurement with your target using the same endpoints and units. If the tape begins away from zero, the garment is folded or the endpoints are not visible, request a clearer measurement instead of accepting a precise-looking number. Record whether the remaining uncertainty would change your size choice.

Approve only after the evidence answers the question that matters to you. If it does not, request the missing detail or check the current return options promptly. Keep the original packaging while deciding, and finish the decision before adding the item to a consolidated parcel. The photo is evidence for this particular order; it is not a universal size chart for future purchases.

articles.title: Pikobuy Haul Budget: Add Up the Cost Before Buying
articles.description: Build a realistic Pikobuy haul budget by separating item prices, shipping, possible charges and unknown costs, using a clearly labelled planning example.
articles.intro: The sum of your spreadsheet prices is only the beginning of a Pikobuy haul budget. A useful estimate shows which costs are known, which depend on the finished parcel and which still need checking. It also tells you whether there is enough room in your budget for uncertainty. The method below is a planning worksheet, not a quotation or a claim about current Pikobuy fees.

sections.heading: 1. Separate the purchase from the parcel
paragraphs: Pikobuy's published process separates purchasing payment from international shipping payment. Reflect that distinction in your budget. One part records what you need to acquire the selected products; another records what it may take to get the resulting parcel to you.

Start with exact quantities and selected options. A low displayed price may belong to a different variation from the one you intend to order. Record a quote date and currency beside each amount. That makes it easier to identify why the budget changes when a product, option or exchange conversion is updated.

sections.heading: 2. List the charges attached to purchasing
paragraphs: Create separate lines for products, any displayed domestic delivery charge, and any service or payment charges actually shown for your transaction. Do not insert a fee simply because another shopper paid it, and do not assume an unlisted charge is zero.

If several items share one delivery charge, avoid counting it again for every row. Conversely, purchases from separate sellers may not share the same charge. Keep enough detail to reconcile the worksheet with the amount you are asked to pay. A tidy grand total is less useful than a slightly longer table you can explain.

sections.heading: 3. Record the assumptions behind shipping
paragraphs: Treat an early shipping estimate as a scenario. Record the assumed destination, product type, packed weight and dimensions, then keep the estimate date and any route conditions beside the amount. If those inputs change, the earlier number may no longer be a useful comparison.

Do not spread a parcel estimate across items and then mistake that allocation for a carrier tariff. You can divide a planning figure to compare personal value, but the actual parcel quote controls what you pay. A bulky low-priced item may deserve a second look even when its share of the item subtotal is small.

sections.heading: 4. Keep possible destination costs visible
paragraphs: Possible duties, taxes, handling or brokerage charges deserve their own line. Check the requirements for your destination and the terms of the shipping option. This guide does not supply a jurisdiction-specific rate or assume that a route label settles every charge.

Use unknown when you have not established the amount. A blank cell is too easily read as zero. Similarly, a coupon that you have not checked against your parcel should remain a possible adjustment rather than a guaranteed saving. Confirm eligibility, limits and the payable total before using a discount to justify the purchase.

sections.heading: 5. Build a hypothetical planning total
paragraphs: Every value below is invented and expressed in one example currency. The table demonstrates the calculation; it is not a current product price, shipping rate or fee schedule. Notice that the arithmetic subtotal is still incomplete because destination charges have not been established.

In this example, 120 covers the listed assumptions and the chosen reserve. It does not establish an all-inclusive final cost. If the spending limit is 120, the unknown destination line means the purchase has not yet been shown to fit that limit.

sections.heading: 6. Compare useful scenarios
paragraphs: Use scenarios to test the assumptions most likely to change your decision. Compare the parcel with and without a bulky optional item, or compare two packing arrangements using the same destination and product type. Change one factor at a time so you understand what caused the difference.

A personal reserve is a planning choice, not a prediction that charges will rise by that amount. Set it according to how much uncertainty remains and what you can afford. If a modest increase would make the purchase unaffordable, reduce the shortlist before committing to the product stage.

sections.heading: 7. Update the worksheet at each commitment
paragraphs: Replace estimates with confirmed amounts as they become available. Preserve the original estimate beside the replacement if you want to understand which assumptions were inaccurate. Before shipping, check that the budget includes the actual item set and the packaging you requested.

If the total exceeds your limit, identify the least useful optional purchase rather than focusing only on the cheapest line. Consider any costs associated with changing the order before assuming you can remove an item freely. The finished worksheet should answer a simple question: what remains payable, what remains uncertain and can you comfortably cover both?

articles.title: Pikobuy Parcel Weight and Dimensions: Compare Packing Choices
articles.description: Compare Pikobuy parcel weight, dimensions and packing choices with a transparent example, then check the route rules and final quote before shipping.
articles.intro: Two parcels with the same scale weight can occupy very different amounts of space. That is why a useful shipping comparison needs both weight and dimensions, together with the billing rules of the available route. The goal is not simply to make the box smaller. It is to compare packing arrangements that protect the contents, suit your needs and produce a quote you understand.

sections.heading: 1. Distinguish the measurements
paragraphs: Item weight describes the product itself. Packed weight includes the contents and the materials used for dispatch. Parcel dimensions describe the outside of the finished package. A route may use a dimensional calculation, actual weight or other rules when determining its charge.

Keep those values separately in your notes. Adding estimated item weights does not establish the finished parcel weight, and measuring a product box does not establish the dimensions of the outer shipping package. Ask which figure you are looking at before entering it into a comparison. Otherwise, accurate arithmetic can still produce a misleading result.

sections.heading: 2. Use consistent estimator inputs
paragraphs: Pikobuy's public estimator includes destination, product type, weight and three dimensions. Keep those inputs consistent when comparing options. Convert measurements carefully and retain the unit labels; a value entered in centimetres when it represents millimetres would radically change the calculation.

Save each set of assumptions with the result and date. If you change the destination, product classification or route as well as the packaging, you are no longer isolating the effect of the box. That broader comparison can be useful, but label it accurately rather than attributing every difference to repacking.

sections.heading: 3. Understand a dimensional calculation
paragraphs: The following calculation uses an invented divisor of 5,000 cubic centimetres per kilogram to show the arithmetic. It is not a statement of Pikobuy's universal billing rule. In this example, multiply the three outer dimensions and divide the result by 5,000.

For an example box measuring 40 × 30 × 20 cm, the volume is 24,000 cubic centimetres and the illustrative dimensional weight is 4.8 kg. The actual route may specify a different divisor, measurement method, minimum or rounding rule. Read those terms before turning the calculation into a payable-weight assumption.

sections.heading: 4. Compare two hypothetical packing arrangements
paragraphs: Both arrangements below have an assumed scale weight of 3.2 kg, deliberately held constant to isolate the effect of volume. The smaller dimensions are illustrative, not a claim that a warehouse can achieve them for your items.

If a hypothetical route billed the greater of scale and dimensional weight before its own rounding, these examples would start from 4.8 kg and 3.2 kg respectively. That comparison still does not tell you the price or whether the second arrangement is suitable.

rows: Original boxes inside an outer carton
About 3.14 kg using the example divisor

sections.heading: 5. Decide what packaging must preserve
paragraphs: List the functions the packaging serves. A rigid item may need protection from crushing; a structured bag may need support to retain its shape. Small parts need containment so they are not separated from the main item. Original packaging may also matter to you for storage or gifting.

Check any unresolved return question before requesting tags, seals or packaging to be removed. Do not exchange a known requirement for an assumed shipping saving. A useful instruction names the packaging that may change and the protection that must remain, then asks for confirmation of the proposed arrangement.

sections.heading: 6. Compare combining and splitting carefully
paragraphs: Combining items can simplify a shipment, but the combined dimensions and product mix may change the available choices. Splitting can create additional charges or require different packing. Neither approach is automatically cheaper.

Compare complete quotes for the actual alternatives and include any relevant handling charges. Keep destination and service expectations comparable. Check item restrictions and compatibility rather than assuming every product can travel together. Do not treat splitting as a way to obtain a particular customs outcome; that is a separate question governed by the applicable rules and the actual shipment.

sections.heading: 7. Confirm the finished parcel
paragraphs: Before paying, compare the final item list, packed measurements and handling instructions with the version you evaluated. Check the route's charge calculation and any rounding or additional charges that affect the payable total. Save the quote and the choices you accepted.

If the result differs materially from the estimate, identify what changed before approving it. The cause might be a larger outer package, different contents or a route condition. Updating the full haul budget at this point keeps a technically attractive packing choice connected to the practical question of whether the shipment still meets your needs.

articles.title: Pikobuy Shoe Sizing: Compare Foot Length, Labels and Insoles
articles.description: Check Pikobuy shoe sizing by separating foot length, insole measurements and size labels, then use focused evidence to resolve an uncertain fit decision.
articles.intro: Choosing a shoe size from a Pikobuy find requires more than matching the number you usually buy. The label is one part of the record; the seller's measurement method, the model's shape and the evidence for the selected pair are also relevant. This guide helps you compare those references without treating foot length, insole length and outsole length as interchangeable measurements.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the exact shoe option
paragraphs: Save the model or product reference, the selected variation and the size system shown by the listing. A number labelled EU, UK or US needs its accompanying context. If the page provides different charts for different styles, attach the correct chart to your chosen variation.

Check the imported selector against the source before payment. A familiar-looking number can still belong to the wrong system or product version. Do not use another shopper's usual size to settle an unresolved mismatch. First establish what the seller says the selected option means, then decide whether the evidence supports your intended fit.

sections.heading: 2. Build a consistent foot measurement
paragraphs: Measure both feet using one repeatable method, with the same stance and conditions. Record the larger result rather than assuming the measurements are identical. Retain the unit and the method so you can compare the result with the seller's instructions instead of remembering only a rounded number.

Foot length is a starting point for a sizing question, not a complete answer. Width, toe shape and intended socks may affect the available space you need. If the seller provides a method, read it carefully before comparing your measurement. Do not silently substitute a different method because it gives a more convenient size result.

sections.heading: 3. Distinguish the different lengths
paragraphs: A foot measurement describes the wearer. An insole measurement describes a component that may have curves, raised edges or a shape that does not map directly to usable space. An internal measurement attempts to describe space inside the shoe. An outsole measurement includes the outside structure.

Write the measurement type beside every number. Two figures expressed in centimetres are not necessarily comparable. A longer outsole does not establish that your foot will fit, and an insole photograph needs a clear method before it can answer a sizing question. Ask what was measured, from where to where, before interpreting the result.

sections.heading: 4. Account for shape and intended use
paragraphs: Consider the shape of shoes you already find comfortable, while recognising that a different model may behave differently. A narrow toe area can matter even when the length appears suitable. A thick sock can also change how much room is available.

Avoid correcting every concern by choosing a longer size. Extra length may not solve a width problem and can introduce another fit issue. Identify the actual uncertainty, such as forefoot width or the seller's length definition, and ask about that point. If the purchase depends on performance or support that cannot be established remotely, a photograph alone cannot resolve it.

sections.heading: 5. Resolve a hypothetical label mismatch
paragraphs: Imagine that a saved source chart associates one option with a stated foot-length range, while the imported selector displays a different label. The example below deliberately avoids a numerical conversion: the first task is to establish identity, not choose the most familiar number.

rows: Option A with a foot-length range
Save the exact chart and option text
Ask whether it maps to source option A
A readable label on one shoe
Check the second shoe and the confirmed option
Clarify whether it is insole, internal or outsole length

list: Do not infer equivalence from similar labels alone.
Retain the response that explains the mapping.
Pause if the selected option remains ambiguous.

sections.heading: 6. Check evidence for the actual pair
paragraphs: When reviewing warehouse images, connect the visible labels to your selected order. Check both shoes when the distinction matters. If a measurement is needed, specify the requested dimension and ensure the image shows the relevant endpoints and a readable scale.

Ask about the measurement without assuming the item can be handled in any particular way. Removing a component may be inappropriate or unavailable, and a curved component can be difficult to measure consistently. State the question first and confirm the available method. The objective is interpretable evidence, not an apparently precise number produced by an unclear procedure.

sections.heading: 7. Make a fit decision with clear limits
paragraphs: Record whether the evidence is consistent, incomplete or contradictory. Consistent evidence may justify proceeding, but it does not guarantee comfort. An unanswered question should lead to a specific clarification request rather than an optimistic assumption.

If the received option appears wrong or the sizing evidence conflicts with what you ordered, discuss the issue promptly and check the applicable return conditions. Keep tags, seals and packaging intact while you clarify the next step. Once the size decision is resolved, assess shoe-box and parcel packing separately so a shipping preference does not determine the fit conclusion.

articles.title: Pikobuy Bags: Check Capacity, Straps and Construction
articles.description: Compare Pikobuy bags by usable openings, internal dimensions, straps and visible construction, with a practical example for checking what a bag can carry.
articles.intro: A bag can look large in a product photograph and still fail to carry the object you need. External width, usable opening and interior shape answer different questions. Before choosing between Pikobuy bag finds, define what the bag must carry and how you plan to wear it. This approach makes dimensions and inspection photos useful without pretending they can prove long-term durability or material composition.

sections.heading: 1. Start with what must fit
paragraphs: List the objects you expect to carry together. Measure the largest rigid object, including any case or cover you normally use. A laptop in a padded sleeve needs more space than the bare device, and a bottle may require a different interior height from a flat notebook.

Decide which items are essential and which are optional. If the bag cannot accommodate an essential object, attractive hardware does not solve the problem. Also consider access: being able to place an item inside with effort is different from being able to remove it conveniently during everyday use.

sections.heading: 2. Separate outside size from usable space
paragraphs: External dimensions describe the bag's overall envelope. Interior dimensions can be reduced by padding, seams, divided compartments and curved corners. The opening may be narrower still because of the closure or construction.

Record which measurement each listing provides. Do not label an outside width as usable capacity in your notes. For a rigid object, compare the opening and the relevant interior dimensions, including depth where necessary. If the listing only gives a decorative scale photograph, request a measurement of the limiting area rather than estimating centimetres from an unknown person's hand or body.

sections.heading: 3. Check straps and carrying position
paragraphs: A strap's total length and the distance the bag hangs below your shoulder are different measurements. Read the stated method and check whether the adjustment range includes the way you intend to carry it. Handle clearance may matter if you want to hold the bag over a coat.

Look for how the strap attaches and whether it is removable or fixed, if that affects your use. Do not infer an adjustment range from a photograph of one setting. Keep your question practical: can the supplied strap be adjusted to the required length, and does the record clearly describe that length?

sections.heading: 4. Review visible construction and contents
paragraphs: Use photos to inspect areas relevant to the bag's function: seams, attachment points, lining, closure alignment and the opening. Check whether advertised removable straps or other accessories are included in the selected option. An image that shows them elsewhere in a listing does not necessarily establish what your option contains.

Separate a visible observation from a performance claim. A photograph can show a seam or a buckle; it cannot establish a safe carrying load or repeated-use durability. Similarly, appearance alone does not identify material composition. If a specific material is essential, seek suitable product information and record its source.

sections.heading: 5. Compare two hypothetical bags
paragraphs: Suppose your essential rigid object is 30 cm wide and 22 cm high. These invented dimensions show why the largest outside measurement is not enough. Neither candidate is a product recommendation, and the example leaves depth and carrying comfort to be checked separately.

Bag B deserves further research despite its smaller external width. Do not interpret the 1 cm opening difference as a guaranteed comfortable fit: rounded edges, padding and the insertion angle may still matter. A close fit needs better evidence than a broad comparison.

rows: Opening is narrower than the object's width
Worth checking depth, opening shape and ease of access

sections.heading: 6. Consider shape and parcel protection
paragraphs: A structured bag may need support to avoid crushing, while loose straps and small accessories need containment. Identify which parts are vulnerable and what shape you expect the bag to retain. Explain those requirements when discussing packing rather than requesting the smallest possible package without qualification.

Keep the product decision separate from the shipping decision. A low item price does not reveal the cost of a protective parcel, and a smaller package is not automatically suitable. Compare the finished packing dimensions and quote once available. If a return question is unresolved, clarify it before requesting packaging changes.

sections.heading: 7. Make the missing question explicit
paragraphs: End your comparison with a short decision note: suitable based on available dimensions, hold for a specific measurement, or remove because a requirement fails. A useful request might ask for the usable opening with the closure fully open, or for the strap's adjustable range using clearly stated endpoints.

Retain the source, selected option and response with the candidate. When your own item is inspected, compare the relevant evidence with that record. This keeps the decision focused on what the bag must do, while leaving unverified properties such as long-term wear, load capacity and material authenticity outside the conclusion.

articles.title: Pikobuy Warehouse Returns: Timing, Evidence and Costs
articles.description: Prepare a Pikobuy warehouse return request with the order status, relevant evidence and clear questions about eligibility, timing and any applicable charges.
articles.intro: A warehouse return question is easier to handle when you identify the stage of the order, preserve the item and explain the issue clearly. Start that work promptly rather than waiting until you have a perfect collection of photographs. This independent guide helps you organise a request; it does not decide eligibility, promise approval or replace the current policy and the response for your particular order.

sections.heading: 1. Establish where the item is
paragraphs: Check whether the seller has dispatched the item, whether it is at the warehouse or whether it has already left in an international parcel. Record the exact status text and the time shown. Different stages involve different practical questions, so avoid describing every request simply as a refund.

Save the order reference, selected option and payment record. If several items share one order, identify the affected item precisely. A request about a wrong-size top should not leave support guessing whether you mean another top in the same purchase. Keep the information limited to what is needed for that issue.

sections.heading: 2. Check the current application window
paragraphs: Pikobuy's return page specifies a 120-hour warehouse application window and conditional eligibility. Confirm the precise cutoff for your order in the live process or with support. Do not treat a date-only screenshot as enough to calculate an exact deadline.

Record the time and timezone shown in the order record and preserve the acknowledgement of your request. If you are unsure whether the item qualifies, ask promptly rather than assuming that asking later will extend the window. A support conversation is not evidence of an extension unless the applicable process explicitly confirms one. Keep that distinction visible in your notes.

sections.heading: 3. Preserve the evidence and item condition
paragraphs: Keep tags, seals, packaging and accessories intact while the issue is being assessed. Do not request alterations simply to make a photograph look clearer. If an inspection would require opening or removing something, ask about the effect before proceeding.

Save the source listing, selected variation, relevant size chart and the photographs that show the concern. Record which images relate to your own item. A previous buyer's photograph might illustrate what you expected, but the clearest request compares your recorded order with evidence of what was received. Preserve the original files alongside any explanatory annotations.

sections.heading: 4. Describe the issue without overstating it
paragraphs: Separate an option mismatch, a visible defect, an uncertain measurement and a change of mind. These descriptions help explain what you are asking someone to assess. Use observations you can support, such as the visible label differs from the selected size, rather than a broad statement that everything is wrong.
The following matrix is an editorial preparation tool, not an official eligibility table. It shows how the evidence and question change with the issue.

rows: Can this mismatch be reviewed for return?
What evidence is needed to assess this damage?
Can the measurement discrepancy be clarified?
Is a return available and what would it cost?

sections.heading: 5. Make a concise, actionable request
paragraphs: Start with the order reference and affected item. Describe the issue in one or two sentences, then identify the supporting images. State the outcome you are seeking, while leaving room for the actual procedure and eligibility decision.

For example: my order selected the blue version, but the warehouse label and photos appear to show black. I have attached the selected option and the received-item images. Please confirm whether the variation is incorrect and whether a warehouse return can be requested. This is an original wording example, not a claim that a particular result will be approved.

sections.heading: 6. Ask for the complete cost before proceeding
paragraphs: Return charges can affect whether a change-of-mind request makes practical sense. Ask for the components and the total that would apply to your specific item, including any shipping or service charge. Do not calculate the outcome from another customer's experience.

The official page contains inconsistent wording about original shipping charges, so obtain order-specific clarification. Record the quoted cost, who supplied it and any conditions attached. If an expected refund is discussed, distinguish the product amount from charges that may remain payable. Do not assume the full amount originally paid will necessarily be returned.

sections.heading: 7. Follow the case with a clean record
paragraphs: Keep a short timeline of the request, acknowledgements, additional evidence and decisions. Reply to the existing case where appropriate so the context remains together. If support asks for a missing detail, answer that question directly rather than starting a new description of the entire purchase.

Before authorising a step, check that it refers to the correct item and the resolution you understand. Retain confirmation of what was accepted and what still remains pending. A request submitted, a seller response and a completed refund are different events. Recording each separately helps you follow the outcome without mistaking progress for completion.

sections.heading: 8. Resolve returns before consolidation
paragraphs: Keep an item with an unresolved return request separate from your ready-to-ship list. Record the warehouse status timestamp, the problem, supporting photos and the resolution you requested. Check the current policy and the deadline shown for your order; waiting for another seller’s item does not establish an extension.

Before requesting packaging removal or international dispatch, confirm whether the item is approved for shipping or still awaiting a seller decision. Keep labels, seals and required packaging intact while eligibility is being considered. Ask official support for the exact applicable costs rather than assuming that a return is free or that a general example covers your case.

articles.title: Pikobuy Tracking Not Updating? Check the Stage and Next Step
articles.description: Work out why Pikobuy tracking is not updating by identifying the shipment stage, reading the available evidence and preparing a useful support request.
articles.intro: When Pikobuy tracking appears quiet, first establish which movement you are trying to follow. The seller's delivery to the warehouse and the later international parcel are separate stages. An order record, parcel reference and carrier tracking number may also answer different questions. A useful next step depends on the last event you can confirm, rather than the number of days since you first paid for a product.

sections.heading: 1. Identify the movement you are tracking
paragraphs: Write down whether you are waiting for the seller to send an item, for warehouse processing or for an international parcel. Keep the relevant reference beside that stage. Do not assume a number attached to one movement tracks the next one.

If you have several products, distinguish an individual item's progress from the progress of a parcel containing multiple items. One seller's dispatch does not establish that all the contents of your intended parcel are ready. Use the actual order and parcel records to understand what has been submitted, rather than reconstructing the process from memory.

sections.heading: 2. Find the international dispatch event
paragraphs: Pikobuy's guide places its three-day tracking-information statement after parcel dispatch. That starting point matters. Product payment, warehouse arrival and parcel submission are not automatically the same event as international dispatch.

Check the recorded dispatch date before comparing your situation with the published guidance. If the record does not clearly establish that dispatch occurred, ask for clarification rather than treating a missing scan as a carrier delay. Keep any answer with the parcel record. The statement concerns tracking availability; it does not provide a guaranteed arrival date or diagnose the cause of a particular gap.

sections.heading: 3. Read what the latest event actually says
paragraphs: A record that a label or shipment information exists is different from evidence that a carrier physically accepted a parcel. Later events may describe processing, transfer, an attempted delivery or another action. Read the full event text and its timestamp instead of relying only on a coloured progress bar.

Avoid translating unfamiliar status wording into a stronger claim than it supports. If the event names a partner or another carrier, note that information and check whether a relevant reference is supplied. Do not assume a generic internet status glossary defines the exact meaning of every message on your shipment.

sections.heading: 4. Build a short evidence timeline
paragraphs: A simple log helps you distinguish an unchanged event from a new event with similar wording. Copy the wording accurately, keep the displayed time and note where you obtained it. The following is a hypothetical record format, not a real parcel history or an official status dictionary.

rows: Whether a carrier scan is visible
The cause and required action until clarified

sections.heading: 5. Choose the action for the missing evidence
paragraphs: If there is no international parcel reference, start with the platform record. If dispatch is recorded but tracking has not appeared within the published guidance, ask Pikobuy about that parcel. If a carrier event exists but has stopped changing, retain the last confirmed event and check the applicable service information.

For an address or delivery exception, read any requested action carefully and verify it through the legitimate carrier or platform channel. A quiet tracking period does not by itself prove loss, and a reassuring estimate does not prove the parcel is progressing. Keep the question focused on what evidence or action is missing.

sections.heading: 6. Send support the useful details
paragraphs: Include the parcel reference, dispatch date if shown, carrier and tracking number, the latest event and its timestamp. Add a screenshot when it helps preserve wording that might change. State the question you want answered, such as whether a carrier handover has been confirmed.

A concise example is: this parcel shows dispatch on the recorded date, but I cannot find a carrier acceptance event. The current tracking text is attached. Please confirm the last verified movement and whether I need to take any action. Use Pikobuy's official Contact page for the appropriate support route; this independent site cannot inspect your private shipment.

sections.heading: 7. Keep the record through delivery
paragraphs: Update the log when a meaningful event arrives, and avoid interpreting repeated checks of the same page as new evidence. Preserve any instructions or response that changes the expected next action. If a deadline or escalation step is supplied for your case, record it explicitly.

When the parcel arrives, compare the contents with your item list and retained inspection record. Keep the relevant packaging and labels while any discrepancy is being clarified. Tracking completion and a satisfactory contents check are separate observations. A clean record helps you explain either a delivery issue or an item issue without mixing the two.

sections.heading: 8. Quick triage: match the gap to the next action
paragraphs: No dispatch record: check the parcel submission and shipping payment in your account. Dispatch recorded but no tracking information beyond the official guidance: ask Pikobuy to confirm the handover. A carrier event exists but has stopped: retain its exact wording and timestamp and check the service’s current instructions. A delivery exception asks for action: verify the request through the legitimate platform or carrier channel.

Include the parcel reference, actual dispatch date and latest confirmed event in one support request. Do not start the timeline from the product purchase date, and do not interpret the guide’s three-day tracking statement as a delivery guarantee. If your parcel contains several orders, use the consolidated parcel reference for international tracking.

articles.title: Pikobuy Shipping Calculator: Estimate Your Full Parcel Cost
articles.description: Use the Pikobuy shipping calculator with the right weight, dimensions and destination. Compare quotes and separate freight from your total order budget.
articles.intro: A useful Pikobuy shipping estimate starts with a defined parcel, not just a product price or an assumed number of kilograms. Record your destination, the items you intend to send and the packaging you need. Then use the official calculator to compare the options it actually offers. This guide gives you a repeatable worksheet for comparing estimates without treating them as a final bill.

sections.heading: 1. Prepare the inputs that change the estimate
paragraphs: The official estimator asks for a destination, product type, weight in kilograms and length, width and height in centimetres. Start by writing these values in one place. Mark each value as measured or estimated, and keep the date beside it. Before warehouse arrival, a seller’s product weight may exclude retail packaging, padding and the outer parcel. Treat it as a planning input, not the confirmed shipment weight.

Use the actual destination of delivery. The language you are browsing in does not select a shipping country, and a quote shared by another buyer may use different inputs. For a mixed parcel, check how the available product types describe its contents. If a battery, liquid, fragile component or other unusual item does not fit clearly, ask Pikobuy which category and route conditions apply before relying on the result.

sections.heading: 2. Separate freight from the full order budget
paragraphs: Write the product payment and the later international shipping payment on separate lines. Then add any confirmed domestic delivery, optional handling, payment conversion and destination charges as their own entries. Do not add a fee merely because another buyer mentioned it; mark it as unconfirmed until you have evidence for your order. Equally, an empty field should mean unknown, rather than free.

This catalog displays indicative product prices in USD. A price on a card is not an international shipping quote. Keep the currency of each actual payment visible and compare totals in one chosen currency using the rate and payment charge available to you. A favourable product price can still leave too little budget for the finished parcel. Set your maximum complete budget before deciding how many products to buy.

sections.heading: 3. Use packed dimensions, not a guessed shipping rule
paragraphs: Measure or request the outer parcel’s length, width and height after choosing its packaging. Record actual weight separately. Do not assume that a light but bulky parcel will be priced only by its scale weight. Pikobuy’s guide says routes differ in billing methods, so read the method shown for the option you are comparing. This article does not assign a universal volumetric-weight divisor to every route.

As an arithmetic example only, a box measuring 40 × 30 × 20 cm occupies 24,000 cubic centimetres. Reducing its height to 15 cm changes that to 18,000 cubic centimetres. This demonstrates a change in volume, not a promised price reduction. The available route, its billing steps, protective packaging and the final measurements still decide whether the change affects the quote. Do not remove necessary protection just to reproduce a smaller example.

sections.heading: 4. Compare two options with the same parcel
paragraphs: Run your comparison with the same destination, contents and measurements. Record the exact route label and the time you obtained each result. A second quote for a lighter parcel is not evidence that its route is cheaper. If the quote changes while you are adjusting packaging, keep the old inputs so that you can explain the difference instead of attributing it automatically to a new rate.

Use the worksheet below for each candidate. Copy the terms that are actually shown, and ask about missing information before paying. A blank transit estimate or unclear inclusion is a question to resolve. When insurance, handling or another optional service appears, compare the total with the same options selected. The cheapest displayed starting price may not represent the complete service you want.

sections.heading: 5. Compare packaging scenarios without assuming savings
paragraphs: Make one scenario for the packaging you need and another only if a practical alternative is available. For shoes, distinguish keeping the retail box from protecting the shoes themselves. For a fragile item, identify which protection is essential. For clothing, check whether your measurements describe a loosely packed group of items or the parcel the warehouse is actually preparing. These differences should be visible in your notes.

Ask for confirmation before requesting irreversible packaging changes. Tags, seals and original packaging can matter to return eligibility, so resolve any inspection or return decision first. A smaller parcel is not automatically the better outcome if an item becomes harder to protect or return. Record both the requested change and the confirmed result; do not replace a measured value with the number you hoped the warehouse would achieve.

sections.heading: 6. Reconcile the estimate with the final parcel quote
paragraphs: Before paying for international shipping, compare the final parcel record with your worksheet. Check the item list, destination, route, packed weight, dimensions and selected services. If the amount differs, identify the input or charge that changed. An earlier screenshot helps distinguish a new measurement from an option you accidentally selected. Ask for a breakdown when the difference remains unexplained.

Keep the quote, payment confirmation and parcel reference together. They answer different questions: the quote describes the offer, the payment record shows what you paid, and the parcel record connects the shipment to its contents. A successful product payment does not prove that international freight has also been paid. Follow the actual account workflow rather than treating all transactions as one order total.

sections.heading: 7. When the calculator gives no useful result
paragraphs: First check the units, destination and product category. A missing option does not by itself establish that an item can never be shipped, and it does not justify selecting an inaccurate category to force a quote. Save the inputs and ask official support whether the contents and dimensions are eligible for a currently available route. Avoid placing more orders merely to reach a parcel size someone else recommends.

If you are still waiting for warehouse measurements, keep a range of possible budgets in your own planning notes and label the assumptions. Do not publish one provisional result as a standard Pikobuy shipping price. When the missing detail becomes available, replace the assumption and rerun the comparison. This gives you an auditable decision without inventing rates, guaranteed savings or delivery dates.

sections.heading: 8. Finish with a short decision record
paragraphs: Your final record should say which items are included, which inspection questions are resolved, which packaging you approved and why the chosen route fits your needs. Include the full amount and any remaining charges you have been told are excluded. If a cost remains unknown and would break your budget, clarify it before making the next payment.

For a mixed order, use the consolidation guide before finalising the parcel. For destination-specific planning, use the Europe shipping checklist. After dispatch, switch to the tracking guide rather than continuing to use the calculator as evidence of progress. Estimating, buying, inspecting and tracking are connected tasks, but each needs its own evidence.

sections.heading: 9. Worked comparison: change one assumption at a time
paragraphs: A buyer is planning to send two pairs of shoes and a sweatshirt. Before warehouse arrival, the buyer has only item weights from listings and no packed dimensions. The first worksheet therefore marks weight and size as estimates. After QC, the buyer decides to retain one shoe box and asks what packaging is appropriate for the other pair. No price is assumed at this stage.

Once the warehouse provides the resulting parcel measurements, the buyer enters those values in the official calculator and records the available options. If the quote is over budget, the next question is whether a different eligible configuration changes the complete cost. The buyer compares that configuration with the original using the same destination and service assumptions. This example illustrates a method, not an actual order, rate or saving. The key is to identify which input changed before accepting the new result.

articles.title: Pikobuy Shipping to Europe: Destination and Delivery Checklist
articles.description: Plan Pikobuy shipping to the Netherlands, Germany and other European destinations: check route availability, address, parcel costs and tracking stages.
articles.intro: Planning Pikobuy shipping to Europe requires a quote for your actual delivery country and parcel. A guide written in Dutch, German or English cannot establish which routes are available to your account today. Use this destination checklist to prepare the right inputs, compare the options shown by Pikobuy and keep the records you need from warehouse approval through delivery.

sections.heading: 1. Start with the delivery country, not the site language
paragraphs: Select the country where the parcel will be delivered in the official shipping estimator. A buyer shipping to the Netherlands should use that destination even when reading an English guide. Apply the same principle to Germany, France, Spain or another country. The languages on this site help you read the guidance; they do not represent separate carrier contracts or a promise that every route serves every destination.

Record the postcode and the destination details needed for the real parcel submission. Check spelling, house or building number, apartment information where relevant and the recipient’s contact details in the actual form. Do not assume the calculator has validated a complete address simply because it accepted a country. If your address has an unusual format or delivery restriction, resolve that question through the platform before dispatch.

sections.heading: 2. Define the contents before comparing European routes
paragraphs: List every item you intend to send and resolve any warehouse inspection question first. Keep the chosen size, colour and quantity beside the item reference so that a parcel is built from approved items. One item still awaiting a seller response can change when you are ready to submit the whole parcel. A delivery plan based on an incomplete list will become unreliable when the contents change.

Describe any special contents accurately when asking about eligibility. Do not infer permission for a battery, liquid or fragile item from a route name or from another person’s successful delivery. Restrictions and handling depend on the actual service and contents. Ask which current option accepts your parcel, and retain the response with the estimate. An attractive quote is useful only if the parcel can legitimately use that service.

sections.heading: 3. Compare the service shown for your destination
paragraphs: For each available option, save the route name, quoted amount, currency, relevant billing method and any displayed transit estimate. Keep the weight and dimensions unchanged during the comparison. The official guide says routes can differ in time and billing, but it does not establish one universally best route to Europe. Choose from the options currently shown for your own parcel and needs.

Ask what the quoted service includes when the wording is unclear. A route label alone is not enough evidence for every charge, handling step or delivery promise. Do not substitute a social-media price list for the offer in your account. If two results use different packaging or optional services, make those differences explicit before comparing the totals. Keep screenshots dated so that an older quote is not mistaken for a current offer.

sections.heading: 4. Leave room for charges outside the displayed freight
paragraphs: Separate the product cost, domestic delivery, international freight, optional services and any applicable destination charges in your planning sheet. Do not assume the freight figure is the final amount payable for every cross-border order. Equally, do not add an arbitrary percentage or a fee copied from a different destination. Record what the chosen service actually includes and what remains to be confirmed.

For duties, taxes, declarations and local requirements, check the current requirements for the exact delivery destination and the terms of your chosen service. This checklist provides no tax threshold, tax rate or legal exemption. Use accurate contents and values in the required forms; a route name or an informal description from another buyer does not replace those requirements. Ask for clarification when the platform’s wording leaves a material cost uncertain.

sections.heading: 5. Build the timeline from separate milestones
paragraphs: Your overall wait may include seller fulfilment, domestic delivery to the warehouse, inspection, any correction or return decision, parcel preparation and international transport. Keep those stages separate in your notes. An international transit estimate does not automatically include time spent waiting for a seller or for your own approval. For a date-sensitive purchase, evaluate the complete sequence rather than counting only the carrier portion.

Pikobuy’s guide places its tracking-information expectation after dispatch. That is not a three-day delivery promise, and it does not start when you pay for an item. Record the actual dispatch event and follow the tracking reference associated with that parcel. If a stage is unclear, ask what has been completed and what action is still needed instead of inferring progress from the age of the product order.

sections.heading: 6. Use one worksheet per destination and parcel
paragraphs: A separate worksheet prevents information for different recipients or orders from being mixed together. The following fields work for the Netherlands, Germany and other destinations without assuming identical routes or charges. They are a planning template, not verified quotes or a country-by-country delivery table. Complete the fields from your own current records.

If you change the destination, item list or packaging, create a fresh comparison. Preserve the previous version so you can see why the amount or available services changed. This is particularly useful when one friend shares a quote with another: compare the inputs first, then assess whether the example is relevant at all. Never treat the country name alone as a complete parcel specification.

rows: The country and checked address details
Packed weight and three outer dimensions
Current route, total, inclusions and open questions
Parcel reference, dispatch record and last confirmed event

sections.heading: 7. Follow the handover and last delivery stage
paragraphs: After dispatch, read the complete tracking event, timestamp and source. Electronic shipment information is not the same as a physical carrier acceptance scan. If the record identifies a delivery partner or another tracking reference, use the details actually supplied. Do not guess the local carrier from the destination country alone, and do not assume every route follows the same sequence of tracking messages.

For a delivery exception, check the legitimate platform or carrier channel for the requested action. Confirm an address, collection requirement or other instruction only through a verified channel. Keep the exact message and any response. A tracking gap does not by itself prove loss, while an estimated date does not prove the parcel has arrived. Use the tracking troubleshooting article when the evidence stops changing.

sections.heading: 8. Close the loop when the parcel arrives
paragraphs: Compare the received contents with the approved item list and retained inspection photos. Keep the shipping label, packaging and relevant records while any missing or damaged item is being clarified. A delivered tracking status answers a transport question; it does not by itself confirm the contents or their condition.
