Document a specific discrepancy promptly through official support rather than combining several unrelated complaints.

For your next order, review which assumptions changed: packing size, service choice, seller waiting time or an unexpected charge. Update your own planning method, but do not turn one parcel’s experience into a universal delivery guarantee. Starting with current destination inputs, approved contents and an evidence-based timeline makes the next comparison easier without promising a result the available information cannot support.

sections.heading: 9. Worked timeline: separate a seller delay from transport
paragraphs: Consider a hypothetical order intended for delivery in the Netherlands. One garment has reached the warehouse and passed the buyer’s checks, while a second item is still awaiting a seller update. The buyer has not yet submitted an international parcel. Even if the calculator displays a transit estimate, that estimate cannot establish when the incomplete order will arrive at the recipient’s address.

The buyer records the first item’s storage conditions and any unresolved deadline, asks about the second item and compares waiting with shipping only the approved item. After the final parcel is submitted and dispatch is recorded, the buyer begins the international tracking timeline using the parcel reference. If a later carrier event pauses, the support request concerns that event rather than the earlier seller delay. This is a planning example, not a published delivery schedule. Keeping the milestones separate makes both the decision and any support question more precise.

articles.title: Pikobuy Parcel Consolidation: Combine Orders After QC
articles.description: Combine Pikobuy warehouse items with a clear QC, packaging and cost checklist. Compare one parcel with separate shipments without assuming guaranteed savings.
articles.intro: Pikobuy says items from different sellers can be combined into one parcel. The useful question is whether your particular items are ready to travel together, with suitable packaging and a quote you understand. Consolidation should follow your inspection decisions. This guide helps you prepare a clear item list, compare practical packing options and confirm the parcel before paying for international shipping.

sections.heading: 1. Build an item list before choosing a parcel
paragraphs: Record the order reference, product, selected size or colour, quantity and current warehouse status for each item you want to send. Separate received items from those still with a seller or in domestic transit. The fact that one order is ready does not establish that the rest have arrived. Keep a note of any item you plan to exclude so that an old shortlist is not mistaken for the final packing instruction.

For items bought from different sellers, retain the original order references even if they later share one parcel number. These references are useful when you need to explain a missing quantity, a wrong variant or a seller-specific issue. A single international shipment does not erase the separate purchase histories. Your final parcel list should connect each included item to the record you actually checked.

sections.heading: 2. Finish QC and return decisions first
paragraphs: Review the warehouse evidence for the items that have arrived. Match the reference, variant and quantity before looking at visible condition and requested measurements. A catalog photograph is not evidence of the condition of your particular order. If the available photos cannot answer an important question, request the relevant detail through Pikobuy and confirm any charge before deciding to ship the item.

Keep an unresolved item out of the ready-to-ship group until you decide what to do. The published returns policy has timing and eligibility conditions, so waiting for another seller must not distract you from a decision on an item already in the warehouse. Preserve tags, seals and packaging while return eligibility is being clarified. Do not authorise their removal merely to prepare a consolidation estimate.

sections.heading: 3. Decide whether waiting for another item is useful
paragraphs: Compare the practical consequences of waiting with sending the approved items now. Record the missing item, its confirmed status and any relevant deadline shown for the items already stored. The public forwarding terms do not establish one universal free storage period for all orders. Check the current storage conditions for your own items instead of assuming a fixed number of free days from another website.

Waiting may produce a different parcel configuration, but it does not guarantee a saving or a particular dispatch date. A late item can also change the dimensions or the eligible route. If you have a date-sensitive purchase, weigh the complete sequence of remaining steps. Keep the decision simple: which evidence is missing, what deadline matters, and what you will do if the missing item is still not ready.

sections.heading: 4. Give precise packaging instructions
paragraphs: Identify what protection each item needs and which retail packaging you want to retain. Shoes, soft clothing and fragile accessories do not necessarily need identical handling. If you are considering removing a box, specify the item and confirm that the inspection or return decision is complete first. Avoid vague instructions such as removing all packaging when different items have different requirements.

Pikobuy’s shopping guide mentions minimal and reinforced packaging requests. Confirm what is available for your parcel and whether the service changes the charge or dimensions. A request is not proof that the finished parcel has the dimensions you expected. Ask for the resulting packed measurements when they become available, and compare those with the numbers used in your earlier estimate.

sections.heading: 5. Compare one parcel with realistic alternatives
paragraphs: Compare the quote for the approved combined parcel with the total of the separate parcels you would actually send. Use the same destination and a clear list of contents for each option. Include the selected packaging and any confirmed handling services. Comparing one complete parcel against only one half of a split shipment will understate the alternative cost.

The table below is a decision worksheet, not evidence that splitting or combining is always cheaper. Fill it with current measurements and quotes. The result depends on the actual eligible routes and their billing methods. Keep product purchase costs separate when they are unchanged between options; the comparison should make the differences visible rather than count the same purchase twice.

sections.heading: 6. Confirm the parcel before payment
paragraphs: Read the final item list and quantities against your own record. Check the delivery address, route, packaging instructions and amount before submitting or paying. If an item is absent, do not assume it will be added automatically because it belongs to the same account. If an unexpected item is included, resolve it before the parcel is dispatched. A clear confirmation is easier than reconstructing your intention later.

Keep the final parcel reference alongside the individual order references. Record what the platform confirms about weight, dimensions and included services. If a total changes after packing, compare it with your earlier estimate and identify the changed input. Ask a focused question about an unexplained difference rather than assuming that the original estimate was a binding final price.

sections.heading: 7. Ask a question that support can act on
paragraphs: A useful request identifies the items, the action you want and the point that needs confirmation. For example: please confirm whether the listed warehouse items can share a parcel to my selected destination, with the stated packaging retained, and advise the resulting weight, dimensions and current shipping options. Replace the general description with your actual references inside the official account channel.

If you are comparing configurations, make clear which item list belongs to each option. If you need a photo before deciding, specify the part or measurement that is missing. Keep account credentials and payment secrets out of messages and public screenshots. This independent guide cannot inspect private orders or issue warehouse instructions on your behalf; use Pikobuy’s official contact route for the decision.

sections.heading: 8. Check the contents as well as the tracking result
paragraphs: Follow the international parcel using its own tracking record after dispatch. A seller’s domestic tracking number does not necessarily track the combined shipment. Preserve the parcel list and inspection evidence through delivery. When the package arrives, compare the contents and quantities with that list before closing your record, especially when several sellers’ items share one outer box.

If something is missing or visibly damaged, document the specific discrepancy and retain relevant labels and packaging while you contact support. Distinguish an item problem from a delivery-status problem. For future planning, note whether consolidation changed the measurements, available routes or handling you needed. Use the result to improve your own checklist, without treating one order as proof of universal savings.

sections.heading: 9. Worked item list: keep one unresolved item separate
paragraphs: Imagine that a buyer has ordered a T-shirt, a pair of shoes and a small bag from three sellers. The T-shirt’s size and condition have been checked. The shoes need an additional measurement, and the bag has not reached the warehouse. The ready list contains only the T-shirt; it should not silently include the other two items simply because all three were purchased for the same planned shipment.

The buyer requests the shoe measurement, checks the bag’s latest confirmed status and records the storage and return conditions relevant to the arrived items. After receiving enough evidence, the buyer can compare a parcel of approved items with a later alternative that includes the bag. Each option needs its own actual contents and measurements. This hypothetical example does not recommend waiting or splitting in every case. It shows why an explicit item list is more useful than a general instruction to combine everything in the account.

qc.title: Pikobuy QC Guide: Photos, Measurements & Returns
qc.description: Check Pikobuy QC photos against your order: size, colour, quantity and visible condition. Learn when to request more evidence before shipping.

sections.heading: Match the photos to your own order
paragraphs: Start with the order reference, selected variant and quantity. Compare the warehouse record with the product you actually bought, not a similar listing. Images in this independent catalog are product photos; they are not linked QC evidence for your order.

sections.heading: Check visible details and measurements
paragraphs: Review colour, labels, seams, print placement, accessories and visible damage. For sizing, request the specific measurement that affects your decision, using the same method as the seller’s chart. A clear label does not establish fit, and a photograph does not establish material composition, authenticity or long-term performance.

sections.heading: Request the detail that would change your decision
paragraphs: State which item and which part must be shown. For example, ask for the garment laid flat with the measuring tape visible from edge to edge. Confirm the available service and fee within Pikobuy. If a photo remains inconclusive, keep that uncertainty visible instead of treating it as approval.

sections.heading: Decide before parcel submission
paragraphs: Approve the item, request clarification or pursue an eligible return while the item is still in the warehouse. Check the current return conditions promptly and preserve required packaging. Complete this decision before consolidation or irreversible packaging changes. Keep the inspection record with your final parcel list.

shipping.title: Pikobuy Shipping: Calculator, Costs & Tracking
shipping.description: Plan Pikobuy shipping with the official calculator, packed weight and dimensions. Compare routes, combine approved items and follow tracking after dispatch.

sections.heading: Estimate the parcel before committing your budget
paragraphs: Use the official calculator with the actual delivery country, product type, weight and three dimensions. Keep measured values separate from guesses. Compare the same parcel across the available options and save the date, currency, route and included services with each result.

sections.heading: Separate product payment and international freight
paragraphs: A catalog price is an indicative product price in USD. It excludes international shipping and possible additional charges. Keep the purchasing payment, shipping payment and any confirmed optional or destination costs in separate budget lines. Clarify an unknown amount instead of treating it as zero.

sections.heading: Choose packaging after QC
paragraphs: Resolve sizing and condition questions before combining warehouse items. Check whether packaging changes affect protection or a possible return. Compare the finished parcel’s weight and dimensions with the values used in the estimate; do not assume that combining items always reduces the total.

sections.heading: Track the shipment from its actual dispatch
paragraphs: The official guide’s three-day statement concerns tracking information after dispatch, not delivery within three days. Distinguish product payment, warehouse arrival, parcel submission and carrier movement. Keep the parcel reference and last confirmed event when asking support about a missing update.
